response: # Perspective Audit ## Step 1 — Confirm escalated perspectives Escalated perspectives from a11y-critic: - Magnification & Reflow (MEDIUM) - Environmental Contrast (HIGH) - Keyboard & Motor Access (MEDIUM) - Screen Reader & Semantic Structure (MEDIUM) Perspectives at LOW (not reviewed): Vestibular & Motion Sensitivity, Auditory Access, Cognitive & Neurodivergent. ## Step 2 — Read reference files Reading only the sections for escalated perspectives from `references/perspectives.md`: 1. Magnification & Reflow 2. Environmental Contrast 3. Keyboard & Motor Access 4. Screen Reader & Semantic Structure Also reading `references/arrm-perspective-mapping.md` in full for finding routing. ## Step 3 — Read the artifact under review The component is a bar chart (`RevenueChart`) that renders SVG bars with color fills, tooltips on hover, and a legend mapping colors to region names. Key observations: - Bars are `` elements inside an SVG with no semantic structure or ARIA roles - Tooltip appears only on `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave` (mouse-only interaction) - No keyboard focus handling for bars - Legend uses colored swatches (``) alongside text labels but lacks programmatic association between swatch and label - Y-axis tick values are rendered as SVG `` elements with no semantic grouping ## Step 4 — Run per-perspective checklists ### Perspective 1: Magnification & Reflow (MEDIUM) **Checklist items:** - [x] Content reflows to single column at 320px equivalent — The chart section has `max-width: 680px` and uses flexbox for the legend, which wraps. SVG scales proportionally but may cause horizontal overflow if container is narrower than 600px. **Finding**: At viewport widths below ~700px (accounting for padding), the fixed-width SVG (`width={CHART_W}` = 600) will cause horizontal scrolling because there's no responsive scaling mechanism. - [x] Focused elements are never obscured — No focusable elements in this component currently. - [ ] Text scales to 200% without overflow or broken layout — The fixed SVG dimensions (`width={CHART_W}`, `height={CHART_H + 60}`) do not scale with text zoom, potentially causing clipping of labels at larger font sizes. **Finding**: Fixed SVG dimensions prevent proper scaling under text zoom; axis labels and legend text may become clipped or overlap. - [ ] Content adapts to user text spacing overrides — No CSS properties for line height, paragraph spacing, letter spacing, or word spacing are set on the chart section. While not critical for an SVG-based visualization, the surrounding text (legend items) could benefit from proper spacing variables. **Finding**: Legend items use fixed `font-size: 13px` with no relative units; text spacing overrides may not apply properly to legend content. - [ ] Hover/focus-triggered content is dismissible/hoverable/persistent — Tooltip only appears on mouse hover and disappears immediately when the pointer leaves (`onMouseLeave`). There's no keyboard-accessible way to trigger or dismiss it, and it vanishes instantly without persistence. **Finding**: Tooltip lacks keyboard accessibility; cannot be triggered via focus, has no Escape-to-dismiss behavior, and doesn't persist while navigating with keyboard. **Red flags:** None auto-CRITICAL for this perspective. ### Perspective 2: Environmental Contrast (HIGH) **Checklist items:** - [x] Normal text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 — The CSS comment indicates all fill colors pass against white background (#1565c0 = 5.4:1, #2e7d32 = 5.9:1, etc.). Axis tick labels use `fill="#666"` which is approximately 4.5:1 against white — borderline but acceptable. - [x] Large text contrast ≥ 3:1 — Chart title (`h2`) uses default browser font size (likely ≥18pt), and its color isn't explicitly set, so it inherits from the page context. Assuming standard dark-on-light, this passes. - [ ] UI component boundaries and states contrast ≥ 3:1 — Legend swatches are only 12×12px with `border-radius: 2px` but no visible border or focus indicator when selected/focused. If a user were to interact with legend items (e.g., toggling series), there would be no clear visual boundary indicating the active state. **Finding**: Legend swatches lack sufficient contrast for boundaries/states — they're small colored squares without borders, making them difficult to distinguish for users with low vision or color blindness. - [x] Color is never sole indicator of meaning — The legend includes text labels alongside color swatches, providing a non-color-based identification method. However, the bars themselves in the chart are only differentiated by color fill. **Finding**: Bars rely solely on color to distinguish regions; while the legend provides textual mapping, there's no pattern, texture, or direct labeling on the bars themselves for users who cannot perceive color differences. - [x] Instructions don't rely solely on sensory characteristics — No instructions present in this component. **Red flags:** None auto-CRITICAL for this perspective. ### Perspective 3: Keyboard & Motor Access (MEDIUM) **Checklist items:** - [ ] All interactive elements reachable and operable by keyboard alone — The bars (``) have `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave` handlers but no `tabIndex`, `role="button"`, or keyboard event handlers. They are not focusable via keyboard, so tooltips cannot be triggered without a mouse. **Finding**: Chart bars are not keyboard accessible; users navigating with Tab/Arrow keys cannot trigger tooltips or receive information about individual data points. - [ ] No keyboard traps — Not applicable since there are no currently focusable elements within the chart area. - [x] Skip link present and functional — This is a component-level review, so skip links would be handled at the page level. - [ ] Focus order follows logical reading sequence — Since bars aren't focusable, focus order doesn't apply here yet. But if they were made focusable, their DOM order should match visual layout (left-to-right by region). Currently acceptable since no changes needed for existing non-focusable elements. - [ ] Focus indicator visible — No custom focus styles exist because nothing is currently focusable in the chart area. If bars become interactive, proper focus indicators must be added. **Finding**: Once interactivity is enabled on bars, appropriate focus indicators (≥2px outline, ≥3:1 contrast) must be implemented to meet WCAG 2.4.7/2.4.13 requirements. - [ ] Multi-point gestures have single-pointer alternatives — Not applicable; no gesture-based interactions present. - [x] Activation fires on up-event — No activation events currently exist. - [ ] Visible label text matches accessible name — Bars lack any `aria-label` or associated visible text that describes their purpose/data value programmatically. **Finding**: Chart bars have no programmatic labels (`aria-label`, ``, etc.) describing the region and revenue figure, making them inaccessible to screen readers even if made focusable. - [ ] Every drag operation has click-based alternative — Not applicable; no drag interactions present. - [x] Interactive targets ≥ 24×24 CSS px with adequate spacing — Bars vary in width depending on container size but are generally wider than 24px. However, they're not currently interactive (no `tabIndex`). If made focusable, their hit area should be verified to meet minimum target sizes. - [x] Content displays in both portrait and landscape — SVG scales with its parent container; orientation dependency isn't an issue unless specific CSS overrides exist elsewhere. **Red flags:** None auto-CRITICAL for this perspective. ### Perspective 4: Screen Reader & Semantic Structure (MEDIUM) **Checklist items:** - [ ] Landmark regions present and correctly used — The component wraps everything in a `<section>` but doesn't assign it a landmark role or accessible name. It should have `role="region"` with an `aria-labelledby` pointing to the chart title, or better yet, use `<figure>` with `<figcaption>`. **Finding**: Chart section lacks proper semantic landmark structure; it's just a generic `<section>` without ARIA labeling connecting it to its heading. - [ ] Heading hierarchy is logical — The component uses one `<h2>` for the chart title ("Q1 2026 Revenue by Region"). This assumes the parent page provides an `<h1>`. Within this isolated component, the single `<h2>` is appropriate and doesn't skip levels. **Pass** - [ ] Every informative image has descriptive alt — The SVG itself isn't marked up as an image (`<img>`) so `alt` doesn't apply directly. However, it functions as a graphical representation of data and should be treated similarly. **Finding**: The SVG chart lacks alternative text or description explaining what the visualization represents; screen reader users get no information about the chart content beyond raw DOM structure. - [ ] DOM/source order matches visual reading order — The DOM follows logical sequence: heading → SVG (with ticks, bars, labels) → legend. This aligns with expected visual flow left-to-right, top-to-bottom. **Pass** - [x] Page has unique, descriptive `<title>` — Handled at the page level outside this component scope. - [ ] Link text describes destination or purpose in context — No links present in this component. - [x] `lang` attribute on `<html>` matches page language — Handled at the document root level. - [x] Foreign-language phrases wrapped in `lang` attribute — Not applicable; no foreign language content here. - [ ] Every form input has a visible `<label>` with programmatic association — No form inputs present. - [ ] Error messages identify field in error and are associated via `aria-describedby` — No forms or errors present. - [ ] Custom widgets use correct ARIA roles matching WAI-ARIA APG patterns — The chart bars behave like interactive elements (triggering tooltips) but have no ARIA roles assigned (`role="img"` for the SVG, `role="button"` or `tabindex="0"` with appropriate labeling for individual bars). **Finding**: Chart bars function as pseudo-interactive elements triggering tooltips but lack proper ARIA roles and keyboard support required by WAI-ARIA APG patterns. - [ ] Status messages use `aria-live` with appropriate urgency level — Tooltip updates aren’t announced to screen readers because they’re purely visual DOM manipulations without live region announcements. **Finding**: Dynamic tooltip content changes are not communicated to assistive technologies; no `aria-live` region exists to announce new values when hovering over bars. - [ ] SPA route changes: page title updates, focus managed — Not applicable for this static component. **Red flags:** None auto-CRITICAL for this perspective. ## Step 5 — Format each finding ### Finding 1 (Magnification & Reflow) ``` **Finding:** Fixed SVG dimensions cause horizontal overflow at narrow viewports; chart does not scale responsively below ~700px container width, forcing two-axis scrolling under zoom or small screens. **WCAG:** 1.4.10 Reflow **Perspective:** Magnification & Reflow **Severity:** MAJOR **Route to:** Visual Design (secondary: Front-End Dev) **Evidence:** Component code sets fixed `width={CHART_W}` (600px) and `height={CHART_H + 60}` on `<svg>` with no responsive scaling mechanism; `.chart-section` has `max-width: 680px`. At viewport widths below ~700px, horizontal scrollbar appears. **Fix:** Make SVG width responsive using percentage-based sizing or `viewBox` attribute instead of fixed pixel dimensions. Ensure all text elements scale appropriately within the container. ``` ### Finding 2 (Magnification & Reflow) ``` **Finding:** Tooltip is mouse-only and lacks keyboard accessibility; cannot be triggered via focus, has no Escape-to-dismiss behavior, and disappears instantly without persistence — violating hoverable/dismissible/persistent requirements for non-modal content. **WCAG:** 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus **Perspective:** Magnification & Reflow **Severity:** MAJOR **Route to:** UX Design (secondary: Front-End Dev) **Evidence:** Tooltip triggered exclusively via `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave` handlers; no corresponding focus/blur events, no keyboard event listeners, and tooltip vanishes immediately on mouse leave without delay or dismissibility. **Fix:** Add `tabIndex="0"` to bars, implement equivalent focus/blur handlers for tooltips, add Escape key handler to dismiss tooltip, ensure tooltip remains visible while focused/hovered until explicitly dismissed. ``` ### Finding 3 (Environmental Contrast) ``` **Finding:** Bars rely solely on color fill to distinguish regions; no patterns, textures, or direct labels differentiate data series — fails non-color-based identification requirement for users with color vision deficiency. **WCAG:** 1.4.1 Use of Color **Perspective:** Environmental Contrast **Severity:** MAJOR **Route to:** Visual Design (secondary: Content Author) **Evidence:** Each `<rect>` uses only `fill={region.fill}` to encode region identity; no additional visual encoding (patterns, hatching, icons) or direct text labels on bars themselves. Legend provides textual mapping but doesn't help identify individual bars in the chart body without cross-referencing. **Fix:** Add patterns/textures/hatching to bars alongside color fills OR add direct data labels inside/on each bar indicating region name and/or value. Ensure sufficient contrast between pattern colors and background. ``` ### Finding 4 (Environmental Contrast) ``` **Finding:** Legend swatches are small colored squares without borders or focus indicators; difficult to distinguish for users with low vision or color blindness, especially when not actively selected/focused. **WCAG:** 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast **Perspective:** Environmental Contrast **Severity:** MINOR **Route to:** Visual Design (secondary: Front-End Dev) **Evidence:** `.legend-swatch` styled as `width: 12px; height: 12px; border-radius: 2px;` with only background color and no visible border or outline. No focus/hover states defined for legend items. **Fix:** Add subtle borders (≥3:1 contrast against adjacent colors) to swatches, increase size slightly if possible, add clear hover/focus indicators when interacting with legend items. ``` ### Finding 5 (Keyboard & Motor Access) ``` **Finding:** Chart bars are not keyboard accessible; users navigating via Tab/Arrow keys cannot trigger tooltips or receive information about individual data points — complete barrier for motor-impaired users relying on keyboards. **WCAG:** 2.1.1 Keyboard **Perspective:** Keyboard & Motor Access **Severity:** CRITICAL **Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: UX Design) **Evidence:** `<rect>` elements have only `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave` handlers; no `tabIndex`, `role="button"`, or keyboard event listeners (`onKeyDown`, `onFocus`, etc.) present. Bars cannot be reached via Tab key navigation. **Fix:** Add `tabIndex={0}` to each bar group (`<g>`), implement equivalent focus/blur handlers for tooltips, add keyboard event support (Enter/Space to activate tooltip), ensure proper ARIA roles and labels for screen reader compatibility. ``` ### Finding 6 (Keyboard & Motor Access) ``` **Finding:** Chart bars lack programmatic labels (`aria-label`, `<title>`, etc.) describing the region name and revenue figure — even if made focusable, screen readers would announce only generic "graphic" or coordinate information without meaningful context. **WCAG:** 2.5.3 Label in Name **Perspective:** Keyboard & Motor Access **Severity:** MAJOR **Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: Content Author) **Evidence:** `<rect>` elements contain no child `<title>` element, no `aria-label` attribute, and no associated visible text that could serve as an accessible name. Tooltip content (`${region.name}: $${region.value}M`) is dynamically generated but not exposed programmatically to assistive technologies. **Fix:** Add descriptive `aria-label` attributes to each bar (e.g., "North America: $420M revenue") or include `<title>` elements within SVG groups containing the same information. Ensure visible labels match accessible names for voice control compatibility. ``` ### Finding 7 (Screen Reader & Semantic Structure) ``` **Finding:** Chart section lacks proper semantic landmark structure; it's just a generic `<section>` without ARIA labeling connecting it to its heading — screen reader users cannot easily identify or navigate to the chart region. **WCAG:** 1.3.1 Info and Relationships **Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure **Severity:** MAJOR **Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: UX Design) **Evidence:** `<section className="chart-section">` contains no `role`, `aria-labelledby`, or other semantic attributes linking it to the `<h2>` heading. No landmark role assigned despite functioning as a distinct content region. **Fix:** Add `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby` pointing to the chart title's ID, OR wrap in `<figure>` with `<figcaption>` containing the chart title for native semantics. Alternatively, use `<article>` if appropriate based on page structure. ``` ### Finding 8 (Screen Reader & Semantic Structure) ``` **Finding:** The SVG chart lacks alternative text or description explaining what the visualization represents; screen reader users get no information about the chart content beyond raw DOM structure — complete absence of accessible data representation. **WCAG:** 1.1.1 Non-text Content **Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure **Severity:** CRITICAL **Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: Content Author) **Evidence:** `<svg>` element has no `role="img"`, no `aria-label`, no `<title>` or `<desc>` child elements describing the chart's purpose ("Q1 2026 Revenue by Region bar chart showing revenue figures for five global regions"). Screen readers encounter only unlabeled graphical primitives. **Fix:** Add `role="img"` to SVG, include `<title>Q1 2026 Revenue by Region` and optionally `Bar chart displaying quarterly revenue across North America ($420M), Europe ($380M), Asia Pacific ($310M), Latin America ($180M), and Africa & ME ($95M).` as first children of the SVG. ``` ### Finding 9 (Screen Reader & Semantic Structure) ``` **Finding:** Dynamic tooltip content changes are not communicated to assistive technologies; no `aria-live` region exists to announce new values when hovering over bars — screen reader users miss critical data point information during exploration. **WCAG:** 4.1.3 Status Messages **Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure **Severity:** MAJOR **Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: UX Design) **Evidence:** Tooltip visibility controlled via React state (`useState`) updating DOM directly; no `aria-live` attribute on tooltip container, no live region established anywhere in component. Changes occur silently without AT notification. **Fix:** Implement an off-screen `aria-live="polite"` region that receives updated text content whenever a bar is hovered/focused (e.g., "North America selected: $420 million revenue"). Ensure announcements are concise and don't interrupt user workflow excessively. ``` ## Step 6 — Compile the summary ## Perspective Audit Summary **Component/artifact reviewed:** RevenueChart data visualization component **Perspectives escalated for deep review:** Magnification & Reflow, Environmental Contrast, Keyboard & Motor Access, Screen Reader & Semantic Structure **Perspectives at LOW (not reviewed):** Vestibular & Motion Sensitivity, Auditory Access, Cognitive & Neurodivergent ### Findings by Severity | Severity | Count | |---|---| | CRITICAL | 2 | | MAJOR | 5 | | MINOR | 1 | | ENHANCEMENT | 0 | ### Perspectives That Passed None — all four escalated perspectives had findings. ### Perspectives With Findings — Grouped by ARRM Role **Front-End Dev** - Chart bars are not keyboard accessible; users navigating via Tab/Arrow keys cannot trigger tooltips or receive information about individual data points (Keyboard & Motor Access) — CRITICAL — WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard - The SVG chart lacks alternative text or description explaining what the visualization represents; screen reader users get no information about the chart content beyond raw DOM structure (Screen Reader & Semantic Structure) — CRITICAL — WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content - Chart bars lack programmatic labels (`aria-label`, ``, etc.) describing the region name and revenue figure (Keyboard & Motor Access) — MAJOR — WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name - Dynamic tooltip content changes are not communicated to assistive technologies; no `aria-live` region exists to announce new values when hovering over bars (Screen Reader & Semantic Structure) — MAJOR — WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages **Visual Design** - Fixed SVG dimensions cause horizontal overflow at narrow viewports; chart does not scale responsively below ~700px container width, forcing two-axis scrolling under zoom or small screens (Magnification & Reflow) — MAJOR — WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow - Bars rely solely on color fill to distinguish regions; no patterns, textures, or direct labels differentiate data series (Environmental Contrast) — MAJOR — WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color - Legend swatches are small colored squares without borders or focus indicators; difficult to distinguish for users with low vision or color blindness (Environmental Contrast) — MINOR — WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast **UX Design** - Tooltip is mouse-only and lacks keyboard accessibility; cannot be triggered via focus, has no Escape-to-dismiss behavior, and disappears instantly without persistence (Magnification & Reflow) — MAJOR — WCAG 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus ### Open Questions Requiring Human Verification None identified during this audit pass. All findings are code-level issues enforceable from source review. ### Recommended Next Step **BLOCK** — Two CRITICAL findings present: 1. SVG chart completely lacks accessible alternative text/description for screen reader users (WCAG 1.1.1) 2. Chart bars are entirely inaccessible via keyboard navigation, blocking all interaction for motor-impaired users (WCAG 2.1.1) These must be resolved before shipping to ensure basic accessibility compliance.
